spots.name: Villa Tugendhat

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Villa Tugendhat is an architecturally significant building in Brno, Czech Republic. It is one of the pioneering prototypes of modern architecture in Europe, and was designed by the German architects Ludwig Mies van der Rohe and Lilly Reich.

spots.name: Brno astronomical clock
spots.summary: The Brno astronomical clock is a black stone monument in Brno, Czech Republic. It is situated at Náměstí Svobody, the main square in the Brno City Centre. The monument was proposed by the mayor of Brno, Roman Onderka, and it was created by Oldřich Rujbr and Petr Kameník.

spots.name: cathedral of St. Peter and Paul
spots.summary: The Cathedral of Saints Peter and Paul is a Roman Catholic cathedral located on the Petrov hill in the Brno-střed district of the city of Brno in the Czech Republic. It is commonly referred to locally as simply "Petrov".
spots.wikipediaTitle: Cathedral of St. Peter and Paul, Brno

spots.name: Špilberk Castle
spots.summary: Špilberk Castle is a castle on the hilltop in Brno, Southern Moravia. Its construction began as early as the first half of the 13th century by the Přemyslid kings and completed by King Ottokar II of Bohemia.

spots.name: Church of St. James
spots.summary: Saint James' church is a late Gothic three-nave hall church situated in James' square in the centre of Brno, in Czech Republic. One of the largest well-preserved Gothic churches in the Czech Republic. Its history starts in the beginning of the 13th century. The church was categorized as a national monument in 1995.

spots.name: Brno hlavní nádraží

hours.note: Closed Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Brno hlavní nádraží is the principal railway station in Brno, the second largest in the Czech Republic. The railway station is situated in the city centre on the site of the former city walls. It is one of the oldest railway stations in the Czech Republic, having been in operation since 1839.

spots.name: Freedom Square
spots.summary: It forms the heart of the city. It's shaped into big reversed "A". Many cultural events take place here and there are always a lot of people here. It is closed for most cars, but trams run through the middle. Also most of the interesting places in the city center are within 10 minutes walk from the Square.

spots.name: Brno Ossuary

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Brno Ossuary is an underground ossuary in Brno, Czech Republic. It was rediscovered in 2001 in the historical centre of the city, partially under the Church of St. James.

spots.summary: The Church of Saint Thomas and the Annunciation is a historic church in Brno, Czech Republic.

spots.name: AZ Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The AZ Tower is a skyscraper in the city of Brno, Czech Republic. The tower is 111 m (364 ft) tall, and it has 30 floors. It is currently the tallest building in the Czech Republic. Construction of the building commenced in 2011 and completed in April 2013. The building has a floor area of over 17,000 m2 (180,000 ft2).

spots.name: Old Town Hall (Brno)
spots.summary: See beloved Brno symbols the Brno Dragon (Brněnský drak) and the Wheel. Also notice the lopsided tower above the entrance. Legend has it that the city council stiffed the mason who built it and he made the crooked ornament in a fit of pique. The town hall's tower is accessible, but cathedral towers offer much better views for significantly lower price.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Basilica of the Assumption of Our Lady in Old Brno Abbey is a high Gothic, monumental convent temple. It was founded in 980-1020 by the unknown lord or monarch in Moravia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Basilica of the Assumption of Our Lady, Brno

spots.name: Red Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Red Church is a Protestant Church in Brno, Czech Republic. It was designed by architect Heinrich von Ferstel and built up between 1863 and 1867. Nowadays it is used by the Evangelical Church of Czech Brethren. The building is a cultural monument.

spots.name: St Thomas's Abbey, Brno

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Thomas's Abbey is an Augustinian abbey and church located in Brno in the Czech Republic. The geneticist and abbot Gregor Mendel was its most famous religious leader to date, who between 1856 and 1863 conducted his experiments on pea plants in the monastery garden.

spots.name: Brno Exhibition Centre
spots.summary: Brno Exhibition Center is a convention centre based in Brno, Czech Republic. It was established in 1928.

spots.name: Moravian Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: Moravské zemské muzeum is a museum in Brno in the Czech Republic. It is the second-largest and second-oldest museum in the country. Its collections include several million objects from many fields of science and culture.

spots.name: Capuchin Crypt in Brno
spots.summary: The Capuchin Crypt in Brno is a funeral room mainly for Capuchin friars. The crypt was founded in the mid 17th century in the basement of the Capuchin Monastery in the historical centre of Brno.

spots.name: Villa Stiassni
spots.summary: It was built between 1927-1929 for the family textile factory owner Alfred Stiassni. It was later a government villa that hosted many important state visits, such as President Edvard Beneš or Cuban leader Fidel Castro.

spots.name: Moravian Gallery in Brno

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: The Moravian Gallery in Brno is the second largest art museum in the Czech Republic, established in 1961 by the merging of two older institutions. It is in five buildings: Pražák Palace, Governor's Palace, Museum of Applied Arts, Jurkovič House and Josef Hoffmann Museum.

spots.summary: The biggest square in Brno, it's dominated by the Church of Saint Thomas, which is the last resting place of Jobs of Moravia, German King and Margrave of Moravia. The nearby former Governor's Palace offers permanent exhibitions of the Moravian Gallery.

spots.name: Mahen Theatre
spots.summary: Mahen Theatre is a Czech theatre situated in the city of Brno. Mahen Theatre, built as German Deutsches Stadttheater in 1882, was one of the first public buildings in the world lit entirely by electric light. It was built in a combination of Neo-Renaissance, Neo-Baroque and Neoclassical architectural styles.

spots.name: Lužánky
spots.summary: Lužánky is the largest city park in Brno and the oldest municipal park in the Czech Republic. The park is located in the Brno-střed District and covers an area of 22.3 hectares.

spots.name: Denisovy sady
spots.summary: It's one of the most beautiful parks in Brno, with an obelisk and a colonnade, and it offers a nice view of the city, including the Špilberk castle and the cathedral, also it is the oldest public park in the country which was founded by public administration authorities. It's located in the historical center, between the Cathedral of St. Peter and Paul and the Špilberk Castle.

spots.name: Reduta Theatre
spots.summary: The Reduta Theatre is a theatre in Brno, Czech Republic. It was built on the city's oldest square and began its life in Renaissance times as the Taverna (Tavern) Theatre. In 1767, Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart performed with his sister in a concert there. It is now part of the National Theatre in Brno.

spots.name: Brno Central Cemetery
spots.summary: Brno Central Cemetery is a graveyard in Brno, Czech Republic. It is the second largest cemetery in the Czech Republic with an area of 43.3 ha. It was opened in 1883.

spots.summary: Brno City Theatre is a repertoire theatre in Brno, Czech Republic, that focuses on dramatic and music production, mainly musical theatre.
